subsystems.name: Nitrogenase enzyme
subsystems.role: the catalyst that splits the very strong triple bond in N₂ and joins the atoms into ammonia.
parts: Fe protein (the electron donor and ATP-driven switch)

subsystems.name: Metal-cluster assembly line
subsystems.role: builds and inserts the complex iron–molybdenum cofactor the enzyme needs.

subsystems.name: Expression construct
subsystems.role: the engineered DNA that makes a plant cell read the bacterial genes.
parts: codon-optimised gene cluster (roughly 20 genes in free-living bacteria)

subsystems.name: Oxygen protection
subsystems.role: nitrogenase is destroyed by oxygen, yet photosynthesis and respiration make it.

subsystems.name: Energy and electron supply
subsystems.role: nitrogen fixation is expensive: about 16 ATP molecules per N₂ fixed.

subsystems.name: Nitrogen sensing and regulation
subsystems.role: switches fixation on only when the plant is short of nitrogen.

buildSteps.title: Choose the gene set
buildSteps.detail: Select the full nitrogen-fixation gene cluster from a free-living soil bacterium, not just the two enzyme genes — the cofactor machinery is the hard part.

buildSteps.title: Rewrite the genes for a plant
buildSteps.detail: Recode the bacterial DNA for plant codon usage, remove unwanted control sequences, and split the cluster into modules that can be assembled and tested separately.

buildSteps.title: Pick a compartment
buildSteps.detail: Target the proteins either to chloroplasts, where photosynthesis supplies energy and electrons, or to mitochondria, where oxygen is consumed and the low-oxygen environment suits the enzyme.

buildSteps.title: Engineer oxygen protection
buildSteps.detail: Design a compartment or a protective mechanism that keeps oxygen away from the enzyme — in nature this ranges from thick cell walls to dedicated shielding proteins.

buildSteps.title: Wire up energy and electrons
buildSteps.detail: Provide ATP and reducing power from the plant's own metabolism, and accept that this diverts carbon and energy away from grain filling.

buildSteps.title: Build the cofactor supply
buildSteps.detail: Co-express the proteins that make and insert the iron–molybdenum cofactor, and ensure the cell supplies enough iron, sulphur and molybdenum.

buildSteps.title: Test in model systems
buildSteps.detail: Express the pathway first in yeast and tobacco, measuring nitrogenase activity with the standard acetylene-reduction assay.

buildSteps.title: Move into a cereal and trial it
buildSteps.detail: Transform maize, wheat or rice, confirm the enzyme works in roots, then run contained and field trials measuring how much fertiliser can be cut without losing yield.

prerequisites.tech: Large multi-gene pathway engineering in plants
prerequisites.why: plants can be transformed reliably, but assembling and co-ordinating roughly twenty genes is far beyond routine practice.
the enzyme, its cofactor and its oxygen sensitivity are well understood — the gap is making it work inside a crop cell.
without protection, oxygen from the plant's own metabolism irreversibly damages the enzyme.
a cereal fixing its own nitrogen would need a large share of its photosynthetic output, which risks a yield penalty.

prerequisites.tech: Regulation and biosafety frameworks for engineered crops and microbes
prerequisites.why: field release of a nitrogen-fixing cereal would need regulatory approval in each market.

pathway.milestone: individual nitrogenase proteins and partial pathways expressed in yeast, tobacco and a few cereals, with activity far below what a crop needs
pathway.unlocks: proof that bacterial fixation genes can survive and function in plant cells.

pathway.milestone: a complete, working nitrogenase reconstituted in a plant cell
pathway.unlocks: the core biological hurdle is cleared; work shifts to efficiency and regulation.

pathway.milestone: cereals in field trials fixing a measurable share of their own nitrogen
pathway.unlocks: realistic estimates of yield penalty and fertiliser savings.

pathway.milestone: commercial varieties that cut synthetic fertiliser use substantially
pathway.unlocks: lower farming costs and much less nitrous-oxide and nitrate pollution.

pathway.milestone: alternative routes mature in parallel — cereals that host nitrogen-fixing bacteria in root nodules, or bacterial and algal biofertilisers applied to soil
pathway.unlocks: several independent ways to reduce fertiliser dependence, in case no single one succeeds.
